summary: Stony Ridge, a 94-foot state ladder tower in Itasca County, was restored and relocated to Anoka County per a county list; the Forest Fire Lookout Association still lists the Itasca County entry as gone.

facts.design: 94-foot Pittsburg Des Moines ladder tower, state tower number 30
facts.status_note: Restored and moved to Anoka County, where a county list says it is privately owned; the Forest Fire Lookout Association still lists the Itasca County entry as gone

access.note: Privately owned at its Anoka County location per the county list; no source read describes public access

events.note: Erected by the state forest service, per the county list's note; the same list's table gives 1932

evidence.supports: 94-foot Pittsburg Des Moines ladder tower, state tower 30
evidence.quote: Stony Ridge, tower #30, was a 94 foot Pittsburg Des Moines ladder tower.

evidence.supports: stood along Highway 65 in George Washington State Forest, Itasca County
evidence.quote: It stood along Highway 65 in George ... Washington State Forest.

evidence.supports: erected in 1934 by the state forest service
evidence.quote: Erected in 1934 by ... the state forest service.

evidence.supports: table date column gives 1932; Mn MFS owner; 94 ft ladder
survey notes spell the name Stoney Ridge
evidence.quote: Survey notes refer to Stoney Ridge.

evidence.supports: now privately owned, restored and relocated to Anoka County
evidence.quote: Now privately owned, restored and ... relocated to Anoka County.

evidence.supports: FFLA list shows Stony Ridge at the Itasca site as Tower Gone

corrections.why: The county list says the tower was restored and relocated to Anoka County, so the record's gone status does not describe the structure; the FFLA gone entry is for the Itasca County site, which the county list places on Highway 65

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The county list's table gives 1932 in its date column; its note says the tower was erected in 1934. The story uses the note's 1934 and says the table differs.
Survey notes spell it Stoney Ridge and the list gives Rock Ridge as another name; the record keeps Stony Ridge, the name the FFLA list uses.

notes_for_editor: The move to Anoka County and the private ownership rest on one sentence in the Itasca county list (Tlkremer, Wikimedia Commons). No Anoka County list was found on Commons, and no second source was found, so the new location is unconfirmed. The built year conflicts within that same list (1932 table, 1934 note). The status correction to relocated is for a human to review; the FFLA list still shows Tower Gone for the Itasca County entry (47.65245, -93.18944), which the county list places on Highway 65. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 6 page reads.
